adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1/100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError when an authorized caller selects `optimized_pagination=true` because `value` is the audit log's datetime, causing the endpoint to return a raw 500 instead of a page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. In the OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key method (line 840), it calls `int(math.floor(value))` or `int(math.ceil(value))` on the value obtained from `getattr(item, self.key)`. When used with audit logs ordered by '-datetime', the key would be 'datetime' and the value would be a datetime object. Calling math.floor() or math.ceil() on a datetime raises TypeError because these functions expect numeric types. The DateTimePaginator (the original paginator) handles datetime values differently, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator doesn't have proper datetime handling, causing a 500 error when optimized_pagination=true is used.
